What is one thing couples should do together at least once?
See something that is truly incredible for the* first* time together, such as the Grand Canyon.

Tackling a big project together. Remodeling your house, building an outbuilding, major landscaping, anything. Just something where you work physically hard together and have something permanent to show for it. The wiped out exhausted sex at the end of the day is great too.
Go on a long car trip. You really get to know someone after two days straight in a car together.

Big plus one to this. Being in new places and doing new things can bring out sides of the person that you haven't seen or haven't seen in a long time.

Drove Chicago to Miami over 3 days with my girlfriend and had an awesome time.

i think a LONG road trip is amazing for building/keeping your friendship togther

SO and i went on a trip that was about 8k miles and made it a point to not have texting/phone calls... we played old school car games, surfed the web to talk about news/ other stuffs, and enjoyed the scenery together, talked about where we want to live when we retire (rural wyoming is sooooo beautiful).. we loved it so much that we are doing it again in 2 years

Have a massive argument. BUT, work through it until you both get to a common ground you can agree upon. You and your partner will not only learn more about each other, but you'll feel invincible if/when you accomplish this.
Skydiving. The adrenalin and endorphins cause you to get very close for like 2 weeks.

Ikea. Nothing will put everything else in perspective like watching the other person make design choices in a facility that takes 3 hours to walk through and provides many options for every setting.

The two of you will get to really experience each others tastes when you are making decisions about items you will be dedicated to for years.

Cooking. If your SO is trying to eat better, or trying to try new foods, cooking them together is a great way to be supportive, as well as working together well as a team.

Cooking more complex things will require teamwork, but the stakes (heh) are relatively low, so it's a good training ground for working together on bigger issues.
Cook together way more than once! It's a great experience to do very regularly.
